detailedExplanation: This topic is verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Biology Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and the corresponding AQA GCSE Biology 8461 content.

A light microscope uses visible light and lenses to produce a magnified image. An electron microscope has a much higher magnification and resolving power, so it reveals much smaller structures in greater detail.

Magnification tells you how many times larger the image is than the real object. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate. A high magnification with poor resolution can produce a large but blurry image.
The units must match before calculating. Important metric relationships include 1 mm = 1000 μm and 1 μm = 1000 nm.
You must understand light vs electron microscopes, magnification vs resolution, use a light microscope, draw biological specimens and calculate magnification/size.
